07 / CRYPTOGRAPHY

ENCODING + HASHING

Practice Base64 encoding/decoding and SHA-256 hashing on text you enter. Learn the difference between encoding and one-way hashing.

LOCAL COMPUTATION

Encoding

Transforms data into another representation and is reversible when you know the scheme. It is not encryption.

Hashing

Produces a fixed-size digest designed to be one-way. Security systems typically store password verifiers using dedicated password-hashing functions rather than plain SHA-256.

TOR / VPN // PRIVACY CONCEPTS

            
Understand the difference

          

        

        CONCEPT LAB
      

      

        

          VPN
          
Creates an encrypted tunnel between your device and a VPN provider.

          Useful for network privacy; the provider becomes part of the trust model.
        

        

          TOR
          
Routes traffic through multiple relays to reduce direct linkability.

          Designed for anonymity properties, but it does not make unsafe behavior safe.
        

        

          HTTPS
          
Encrypts application traffic between your browser and the website.

          Still important whether you use a VPN, Tor, or neither.
        

      

    


    
    

      

        

          { }
          

            
PYTHON / C++ // SECURITY FOUNDATIONS

            
Code-reading lab

          

        

        SAFE EXAMPLES
      

      

        

          
PYTHON // SHA-256 A STRING

          
import hashlib

message = b"training"
digest = hashlib.sha256(message).hexdigest()
print(digest)

        

        

          
C++ // INPUT LENGTH CHECK

          
#include <iostream>
#include <string>

int main() {
    std::string input;
    std::getline(std::cin, input);

    if (input.size() > 64) {
        std::cout << "Input too long";
        return 1;
    }
}

        

      

      

        Learn Python first for automation and analysis. Add C++ later to understand
        memory, compiled programs and lower-level software behavior.
